root_cause.text: In `ksmbd`’s `smb2_open()` durable-reconnect path, `dh_info.fp`/`fp` was reference-counted incorrectly: `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp)` was called before all later error handling and attribute access finished, allowing the durable file object to be freed while still being used.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes early `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp)` calls from the `dh_info.reconnected` path, including after `ksmbd_check_durable_oplock()`, `ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd()`, `ksmbd_override_fsids()`, and `ksmbd_vfs_getattr(&fp->filp->f_path, &stat)`, and instead adds a single `if (dh_info.reconnected) ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp);` at the end of `smb2_open()`, matching the CVE text that early put could lead to UAF when later code accesses `fp` properties like `fp->create_time`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix durable file descriptor lifetime handling in smb2_open reconnect error paths by deferring cleanup to the common exit path.
intent_record.what: In the durable reopen path of smb2_open(), several explicit calls to ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp) / ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp) were removed from the individual error branches after smb2_check_durable_oplock(), ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd(), ksmbd_override_fsids(), and ksmbd_vfs_getattr(); the control flow still jumps to err_out2 on failure.
intent_record.how: This changes ownership handling for the durable file descriptor during the reconnect/open sequence so that the descriptor is not released immediately on those intermediate failures, avoiding premature cleanup before the shared error-exit path handles it. It prevents double-put or use-after-free style lifetime issues around the durable file object during reconnect processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the durable file descriptor after a successful durable handle reconnection in smb2_open().
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added near the end of smb2_open(): if dh_info.reconnected is true, it calls ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp) before freeing name and lc.
intent_record.how: When an SMB2 open operation reconnects an existing durable handle, the code now releases the durable file descriptor reference after the open completes, preventing the handle from remaining pinned in memory or from leaking a reference.

The group directly concerns the durable-reconnect path in smb2_open() and changes when the durable file descriptor is released. That matches the root cause, which was an incorrect early ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp) causing use-after-free during later error handling and attribute access.

candidates.rationale: This releases the durable file object immediately after ksmbd_vfs_getattr(), but the root cause says the durable reconnect path was reference-counted incorrectly and could free the file while later error handling or attribute-related use was still in progress.
These early puts on reconnect/error paths drop the durable file reference before the common exit path, matching the lifetime bug described in the root cause.
This transfers the durable file pointer into fp for subsequent use, so an earlier ksmbd_put_durable_fd on the same object can leave fp dangling during later operations.
This later attribute access uses the durable file through fp; if the reference was dropped too early, this is a use-after-free point consistent with the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early reference drop in the durable-reconnect path can free the durable file object before later error handling and attribute-related use complete, matching the root cause.
This assigns the durable file pointer into fp for subsequent operations; if the object was already put too early, later uses of fp may dereference freed memory.
This attribute access occurs after the premature put and therefore uses the durable file object at the point where the lifetime bug can manifest as a use-after-free.

This later cleanup call is part of the incorrect lifetime handling in the reconnect path; the fix intent was to defer cleanup to the common exit path so the durable file stayed valid through all later processing.
